subject: WellHealth security questionnaire — PII minimization, retention, and KMS attestation
messages:
From: Dana Liu <security@wellhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Security questionnaire: PII handling, retention limits, and KMS attestation

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this call last week. As part of our procurement review for the WellHealth platform integration, I attached our standard Security Questionnaire (version 3) focused on privacy: PII minimization, retention, access controls, and key management. Could you please: 

- Confirm which Redwood storage systems may see WellHealth PII (S3 buckets, DBs, caches).
- Provide your default retention windows and options for customer-configured retention.
- Provide a KMS attestation or the steps to obtain one (we require customer key custody details).
- Share a data flow diagram that highlights where PII is tokenized, cached, or persisted.

Attachments: WellHealth_Security_Questionnaire_v3.xlsx (Excel questionnaire)

We are hoping to complete the review by 2026-12-20. If it helps, we can schedule a 30-minute follow-up to walk through the evidence links.

Thanks,
Dana Liu
Security Manager, WellHealth Inc.
security@wellhealth.com

Hi Dana —

Thanks for sending this through. We can deliver the questionnaire responses plus supporting artifacts by EOD Tuesday (2026-12-15). Preliminary notes:

- Scope: please confirm whether the scope is only Redwood-hosted production endpoints or if your contract will include Dedicated/Private deployments (that changes subprocessor and custody answers).
- KMS: we have both Redwood-managed KMS for hosted customers and customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private customers; I can provide a standard attestation for our managed KMS and a configuration checklist for customer-managed setups.
- Evidence: I will share a data flow PDF and our current subprocessors CSV; some items may be redacted for vendor confidentiality but we'll add a Drive link for more detailed artifacts.

I'll assemble responses and loop in our Ops leads for the attestation. Would you like a short call on Monday to walk through anything that requires a demo?

Best,
Mina Haddad

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: WellHealth questionnaire — need KMS attestation + dataflow PDF

Mina —

Attached drafts uploaded to the Drive link: redwood_pii_dataflow_v2.pdf and redwood_subprocessors_list.csv. Quick summary of key points (for your consolidation):

- Storage systems that may hold PII: primary object store (internal S3 namespace), production Postgres (encrypted at rest), ephemeral KV caches (encrypted, TTL-managed). We call out tokenization at the ingestion layer for sensitive fields (SSNs, full DOB).
- Retention defaults: logs 30 days, user content 90 days by default; customers can configure retention down to 0 days for ephemeral workloads on Hosted tier via API. Dedicated/Private customers can set retention at deploy time.
- KMS: For hosted customers we use Redwood-managed KMS (multi-tenant, HSM-backed) with per-tenant DEKs; customers can request dedicated key material for an additional control (Dedicated/Private). Attached kms_attestation_draft.txt with suggested wording for our attestation; Sergio please review the operational bits (rotation frequency, escrow, HSM provider).

Attachments (in Drive): redwood_pii_dataflow_v2.pdf, redwood_subprocessors_list.csv, kms_attestation_draft.txt

Marissa
Head of Platform Security, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: WellHealth questionnaire — need KMS attestation + dataflow PDF

Team —

I reviewed Marissa's drafts and made two tweaks to the KMS attestation language regarding rotation windows and key destruction for terminated customers. Key bullets to include in final attestation: 

- Rotation: DEKs rotated every 90 days; KEK rotation policy every 12 months for HSM provider-managed keys.
- Customer-managed keys: documented checklist for bring-your-own-key (BYOK) in Dedicated/Private; we support import or external KMS integration (KMIP / cloud KMS).
- Escrow: we do not escrow keys for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private we can provide escrow under contractual terms.

I uploaded kms_attestation_draft.txt (v2) to the Drive folder and added line edits in the compiled_answers draft.

Sergio
Principal Security Engineer
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
